To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a neural conversational agent that is trained with a large corpus of diverse and high-quality dialogues can achieve state-of-the-art performance on the MultiWOZ dataset and (ii) a bootstrapping approach that combines dialogue self-play and crowdsourcing can be used to generate such a corpus of dialogues for arbitrary tasks.

1) dialogue self-play and crowdsourcing is a promising approach for building a conversational agent for arbitrary tasks; 2) this approach can generate diverse and natural dialogues, and 3) the generated dialogues can be used to train a conversational agent that can achieve good task completion rates.

(1) dialogue self-play can be effectively combined with crowd-sourcing to collect a large corpus of fully-annotated goal-oriented dialogues; (2) a neural model trained on the resulting dataset can perform on-par or better than an agent trained on a manually-annotated dataset of similar size; and (3) interactive learning from users of a conversational agent can be used to improve its performance.
